# ufbx in RestArtEngine

This directory contains unmodified upstream `ufbx.h`, `ufbx.c`, and `LICENSE`
from [ufbx](https://github.com/ufbx/ufbx), version **0.23.1**.

- Release tag: [`v0.23.1`](https://github.com/ufbx/ufbx/tree/v0.23.1)
- Pinned commit: [`26a482ae66871d7de36eb722aa060bce95bce274`](https://github.com/ufbx/ufbx/tree/26a482ae66871d7de36eb722aa060bce95bce274)
- Upstream sources: [header](https://github.com/ufbx/ufbx/blob/26a482ae66871d7de36eb722aa060bce95bce274/ufbx.h), [implementation](https://github.com/ufbx/ufbx/blob/26a482ae66871d7de36eb722aa060bce95bce274/ufbx.c), [license](https://github.com/ufbx/ufbx/blob/26a482ae66871d7de36eb722aa060bce95bce274/LICENSE)
- License used by RestArtEngine: MIT (alternative A in the complete upstream
  dual MIT/public-domain license included alongside these files).

The version is pinned so that builds work offline and use the same parser.
The 0.23.1 release includes upstream malformed-input fixes; preserve the pin
until a newer version has been reviewed and the importer checks have run.
Upstream supports compiling `ufbx.c` as either C or C++; the engine build
compiles it as C++ in its own library or source-file compilation boundary.

The adapter lives in `src/Assets/FbxImporter.cpp`. It loads only an in-memory
FBX document, explicitly forces FBX parsing, refuses external file opens, and
does not extract embedded files or write anything. Binary and ASCII FBX are
handled by the same parser. Temporary and resulting ufbx allocations each have
a 512 MiB limit; input is limited to 256 MiB, hierarchy depth to 256, individual
polygons to 65536 corners, and emitted triangle corners to 12 million. These
are individual bounds, not a process-wide memory quota: input, parser memory,
and the approximately 336 MB maximum output can coexist during conversion.

Current import creates one static mesh containing all mesh node instances in
their default pose. Full hierarchy and geometric transforms are baked into
positions, with inverse-transpose normals and determinant-based winding
correction. The target is left-handed Y-up in meters. Missing normals are
generated by ufbx. The engine stores positions and normals only: UVs, tangents,
vertex colors, materials, textures, animation, skeletons, skinning, blend
shapes, cameras, lights, curves, and subdivision surfaces are not imported.
Skinned meshes contribute their undeformed control mesh at the node's default
transform. Point/line faces are ignored and polygon holes are rejected.
Zero-area output triangles are skipped with a count by default; the import
option can request strict rejection instead. Tiny nonzero-area triangles are
preserved, and an entirely degenerate result is always rejected. Unusable
normals on retained triangles are rebuilt from their geometric cross product
and counted in the import warnings. Invalid indices, non-finite values,
coordinates outside +/-1e9, singular transforms, and empty results fail without
replacing the caller's mesh.
